item.title: India Inflation Risks Mount on Renewed US-Iran Tensions, El Nino
item.description: India’s stronger-than-expected inflation reading for June has left policymakers facing a more uncertain outlook, with renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz threatening to push up oil prices and a developing El Niño raising the risk of higher food costs.

item.title: Finland’s NestAI Builds Sovereign AI Tools for Europe Militaries
item.description: Finnish artificial intelligence lab NestAI Oy is launching an AI engine that the Finnish and Estonian militaries will use to create sovereign models for planning operations and enabling uncrewed autonomous systems.

item.title: Stocks Steady as Oil Extends Gain to $85
India’s Antitrust Body Fines HP $13.3 Million for Cartelizing
item.description: India’s antitrust regulator fined the Indian unit of HP Inc. 1.27 billion rupees ($13.3 million), saying the company colluded with its resellers to rig prices in government procurement tenders.

item.title: Ericsson Sees Higher Quarterly Costs on Network Sales Growth
item.description: Ericsson AB warned that margins for its main networks business will come under pressure this quarter as the Swedish telecommunications maker grapples with higher component costs.

item.title: PE Fund Harith Gets Antitrust Approval to Acquire FlySafair
item.description: South Africa’s antitrust regulator approved private equity firm Harith General Partners’ proposal to acquire budget carrier FlySafair.

item.title: UK’s Miliband Seen as Least Appealing Chancellor: Markets Pulse
item.description: Andy Burnham has yet to announce his choice for UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, but among the presumptive next prime minister’s leading candidates, Energy Secretary Ed Miliband is seen as the least market-friendly choice, according to the latest Bloomberg Markets Live Pulse survey.

item.title: Pure DC Building Finland AI Data Center, Secures Microsoft Deal
item.description: Oaktree Capital Management-backed UK firm Pure Data Centres is building a data center in Finland that clients including Microsoft Corp. are slated to use, part of a broader effort to ramp up the digital infrastructure necessary for Europe to build and run more artificial intelligent systems.

item.title: China’s Green-Tech Exports Surge on Energy Transition Demand
item.description: China’s exports of green-tech products rose by more than a third in the first half of the year, driven by the accelerating global energy transition.

item.title: Indonesia Says S&P Affirmation to Help Stabilize Bond Market
item.description: Indonesia expects S&P Global Ratings’ vote of confidence in its sovereign credit profile to help stabilize the domestic bond market after a selloff in June, according to a top finance ministry official.

item.title: China Expels Former Politburo Member Over Graft and Sex Charges
item.description: China expelled former Politburo member Ma Xingrui from the ruling Communist Party, accusing him of a wide range of offenses including corruption, abuse of power and trading political favors for sex.

item.title: South Korean Won Climbs to Two-Month High on Hynix ADR Inflows
item.description: The South Korean won advanced to its strongest level since May on expectations that dollar inflows from SK Hynix Inc’s American depositary receipts will enter the local currency market.

item.title: Japan’s Power Prices Hit Six-Week High on Heat Wave, Gas Crunch
item.description: Japan’s spot power price climbed to a six-week high as rising temperatures in the capital city lifted consumption, while renewed disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz drove up fuel costs.

item.title: Palm Oil Advances as Crude Rally Boosts Outlook for Biofuels
item.description: Palm oil climbed for a second day as a surge in crude prices fueled by renewed US-Iran hostilities brightened demand prospects for biofuels.

item.title: South Korea Plans FX Rule Easing to Expand Won’s Global Use
item.description: South Korea plans to relax foreign-exchange rules governing capital transactions in the second half of the year as part of a broader effort to internationalize the won and deepen overseas use of the currency.

item.title: US, Iran Check the Oil Price Before Pushing Limits
item.description: Trump’s 20% levy is the latest example of seeing what they can get away with.

item.title: Moonfare Assets Top €4 Billion as PE Platform Draws Rich Clients
item.description: Moonfare’s assets under management topped €4 billion ($4.6 billion) after the private markets investing platform continued to attract inflows from wealthy individuals and family offices.

item.title: Huawei, Apple Get Boost in China From Memory Costs, IDC Says
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co. and Apple Inc. extended their lead atop China’s smartphone market in the June quarter, expanding their shipments as consumers opted to either buy premium devices or skip upgrades, according to IDC.

item.title: DeepSeek’s Liang Tops Amodei and Brockman as Richest AI Founder
item.description: DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng’s net worth more than doubled after his firm’s most recent fundraising round, making the Chinese entrepreneur the world’s richest among creators of AI models.

item.title: Japan Bond Sale Draws High Demand After Katayama’s GPIF Remarks
item.description: Japan’s 20-year government bond auction Tuesday attracted strong investor demand after remarks by Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama boosted sentiment toward sovereign debt.

item.title: Iran Sneaking Out Tankers Via Hormuz as Trump Amps Up Threats
item.description: Iran has been sneaking oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz over the past few days, even before the US said it would reimpose a blockade of Iranian ports as hostilities escalated.

item.title: Yuan Still Cheap Versus Euro Even After Gain, Deutsche Bank Says
item.description: China’s yuan is still undervalued versus the euro despite its recent gains, and that’s contributing to a wider European Union trade deficit, according to Deutsche Bank AG.

item.title: SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son Sees Fusion Power as Key to AI’s Future
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. founder Masayoshi Son said that in the not-so-distant future, nuclear fusion technology will offer the most realistic solution for powering AI data centers’ ballooning needs.

item.title: China’s Crude Oil Imports Plunge to Lowest in Nearly a Decade
item.description: Chinese crude oil imports fell sharply in June to near a decade low, hampered by war in the Persian Gulf and an abrupt slowdown in domestic demand.

item.title: Taiwan Fund Profits 80% After Intervening to Blunt Trump Tariffs
item.description: Taiwan reported a roughly 80% profit from a nine-month-long intervention to support the island’s stock market following the Trump administration’s move to impose tariffs, though it has now exited its position.

item.title: South Korea Turns More Bullish on Economy as Chip Boom Rolls On
item.description: South Korea’s government is taking a more bullish view of the economy than the International Monetary Fund’s recent assessment, maintaining that an artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor boom will continue to outweigh the impact of the Middle East conflict.

item.title: China Exports, Imports Soar Faster Than Forecast as AI Booms
item.description: China’s growth in exports and imports topped all forecasts in June, as surging chip prices and global demand for hardware needed to power AI data centers lift trade across Asia.

item.title: India Large-Caps Eye Comeback on Global Funds’ Support
item.description: Jefferies says large caps are starting to look more reasonably valued.

item.title: Leveraged Chip Bets Backfire in Korea as Biggest ETF Falls 45%
item.description: A new breed of leveraged products tracking major South Korean chip stocks are tumbling in value, threatening steep losses for the country’s retail investors who favor the tools to pursue amplified returns.

item.title: OpenAI’s Feud With xAI Carries On as Apple Secrets Fight Revs Up
item.description: OpenAI asked a judge to find that a lawsuit filed by xAI Corp. accusing the ChatGPT maker of trade secret theft “should never have been filed” and seeks to recoup more than $1 million in legal expenses from Elon Musk’s company.
